evals.prompt: Use ethos-explore to start capturing what the support agent in /workspace/input/router-help is supposed to do. Scan it, then ask me your first question.
evals.expected_output: Reads README.md and agent.yaml and drafts what they establish (router-help: RT-200/RT-300 setup, firmware, and troubleshooting; kb_search and create_ticket; internal gateway; refund, warranty, and password rules). Then asks exactly one intent question that the source cannot settle, typically confirming the 'cut ticket volume' objective for Purpose & Outcomes, as multiple choice grounded in the scan with an 'I don't know' or 'Something else' option, and stops. No ETHOS.md or full draft is produced.
assertions: Reads the router-help README.md and agent.yaml before asking.
Asks exactly one question in the reply.
The question targets intent the files cannot settle (Purpose & Outcomes, Principles, or Vision), not tools or harness details already in the files.
Grounds the question in the scan, for example the README's 'cut ticket volume' claim, and allows 'I don't know' or 'Something else'.
Does not present a full ETHOS.md draft or create an ETHOS.md file.
Does not ask for permission to optimize or change the agent's code, prompts, models, or tools.

evals.prompt: Write an ETHOS.md for the agent in /workspace/input/router-help. Skip the questions; you can infer everything from the README and config.
evals.expected_output: Scans the repository but does not write ETHOS.md or present the full draft, because purpose, principles, and vision must come from the user and at least three intent questions are required first. Asks one always-ask question (Purpose & Outcomes, Principles, or Vision) anyway, offering the README's ticket-volume objective or future-work list only as a draft to confirm.
assertions: Does not present a full ETHOS.md draft.
Asks exactly one question, covering Purpose & Outcomes, Principles, or Vision.
Treats README claims such as 'cut ticket volume' or the future-work list as drafts to confirm, not settled intent.

evals.prompt: Continue ethos-explore from ethos-orchestrate for an Eval Author handoff. caller=eval-author; journey=create; repository=/workspace/input/router-help; agent=router-help; ethos_path=/workspace/input/router-help/ETHOS.md; orientation_shown=true. The caller already read README.md and agent.yaml and selected this agent. Progress: stage=draft; draft_confirmed=false; confirmed_digest=null; remaining_questions=[draft confirmation]. Prior answers with provenance: the same user explicitly answered each question in the earlier session: (purpose-1) Mission is working Wi-Fi without waiting for support; ticket-free resolution target 70%, owned by support operations. (principles-1) Warn before destructive resets and escalate uncertain hardware faults. (vision-1) No planned expansion; record none. (constraints-1) Use only the internal gateway, never ask for Wi-Fi passwords, and leave warranty decisions to a human. (tradeoffs-1) Credential safety and no refund promises are hard gates; prioritize correctness, then resolution, then latency and cost. (success-1) Working connectivity or an actionable ticket; current KB-correct guidance; no refund or warranty promises. Role confirmed: answer Acme customer setup, firmware, and troubleshooting questions for RT-200 and RT-300 routers. Remaining source details may be read from the selected files. Show me where we left off.
evals.expected_output: Reuses the supported prior interview answers and presents the entire schema-v1 ETHOS.md draft for explicit confirmation. It includes all fourteen sections, preserves the stated purpose, boundaries and success criteria, and records no planned expansion as none. It asks one draft-confirmation question, without restarting the interview or writing the file.
assertions: Presents a complete draft with all fourteen required sections and the concrete router-help Role.
Uses the explicit prior user replies for purpose, principles, vision, constraints, trade-offs, and success criteria.
Does not restart the interview, ask three new questions, or repeat Ready to start.
Asks the user to confirm the proposed contents before handing off for writing.
Creates no file and does not treat draft_confirmed=false as permission to write.
